Introduction

Dynamic Duo (often stylized as Dynamicduo) is a South Korean hip hop duo composed of rappers Choiza (Choi Jae-ho) and Gaeko (Kim Yoon-sung), who have been close friends since childhood. The two first entered the Korean hip hop scene in 1999 as members of the trio CB Mass, which released three studio albums before disbanding in 2003 due to internal conflict, after it was revealed that their third member, Curbin, had been embezzling money from the group. The following year, Choiza and Gaeko re-emerged as Dynamic Duo, debuting with the album Taxi Driver (2004). The album was a landmark success in Korean hip hop, selling over 50,000 copies in its first month and becoming the best-selling Korean hip hop album of all time.

Their sophomore album, Double Dynamite, released in 2005, won Best Hip Hop Album at the 2006 Korean Music Awards. In August 2006, the duo co-founded the independent music label Amoeba Culture. The label went on to represent a number of influential hip hop and R&B artists, including Supreme Team, Zion.T, Crush, Primary, Rhythm Power, and Ha:tfelt. Under their label, Dynamic Duo released several more critically and commercially successful albums, such as Enlightened (2007), which featured the award-winning single “Attendance Check,” honored with Best Music Video at the 2007 Mnet Asian Music Awards. This was followed by Last Days (2008) and Band of Dynamic Brothers (2009).

In October 2009, both Choiza and Gaeko enlisted for mandatory military service, completing their basic training together. After completing their service, they returned to music and launched the ‘NOWeekend’ project through Amoeba Culture, an initiative that showcased both their own creative evolution and collaborations with various artists.

Over the years, Dynamic Duo have played a foundational role in the development of Korean hip hop, both as pioneering artists and as industry leaders through their work with Amoeba Culture.
